items.title: Departmental failures found by child protection review of Kumanjayi Little Baby case
items.description: Nearly three months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby, a review into her family circumstances prior to the tragedy has been handed down.

items.title: Job system broken for workers, booming for private equity, report says
items.description: A new report argues Australia's employment services system is failing jobseekers, while filling the pockets of private equity firms and millionaires.

items.title: Teen suspected of stabbing mother to death, injuring sister in Perth
items.description: Police say a teenage boy is suspected to have stabbed his mother to death and seriously injured his 12-year-old sister in an alleged family violence homicide in Perth's south-east.

items.title: 'Don't go there': Pauline Hanson fires up in Q&A over White Australia policy
items.description: Pauline Hanson angrily denies suggestions her strident opposition to migration by anyone from "radical Islamic countries" amounts to a version of the White Australia policy.

items.title: Live: Holocaust survivors have PTSD from antisemitic events, commission hears
items.description: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion is this week focused on security for the Australian Jewish community.

items.title: 'Happening to everybody': AI-manipulated images exploited by scammers
items.description: Papua New Guinea prepares new laws to criminalise the malicious use of artificial intelligence, including deepfakes, voice cloning and digital impersonation.

items.title: PMOS/PCOS linked to 'significantly higher' stroke, heart attack risk
items.description: Women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS, formerly PCOS) have a "significantly higher" risk of cardiovascular disease than those without, a new study suggests.

items.title: Surgeon banned after botched bowel op contributes to patient's death
items.description: A six-month ban on Dr Liu-Ming Schmidt, who works across multiple hospitals in southern NSW, comes after 13 patient complaints including a missed cancer diagnosis and a "catastrophic error" that contributed to a patient's death.

items.title: India steps up response to US, Iran deadly ship strikes
items.description: The Indian government is taking action after 10 sailors were killed and dozens more injured in attacks on commercial cargo ships and oil tankers during the battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: US to impose 50pc tariffs on most Canadian goods
items.description: The White House says the tariffs will go into effect in 30 days, meaning there is time for negotiations.

items.title: Live: ASX falls as oil prices near one-month high on US-Iran escalation
items.description: The Australian share market has fallen after a negative session on Wall Street. Oil prices remain near a one-month high as Yemen's Houthis threaten to impose a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia. See how the trading day unfolds on our blog. Follow live.

items.title: Diplomatic efforts to keep US from cutting ties with UNHCR begin, sources say
items.description: The Trump administration is said to be weighing cutting ties with the UN refugee agency, prompting a campaign for the US to maintain support.

items.title: Anthony Albanese on the night in parliament he would rather not relive
items.description: From left-wing roots to "radical centre" prime minister, Anthony Albanese reflects on his 30-year career in Parliament House.

items.title: Ian doesn't want children. He's part of a growing trend among men
items.description: About 15 per cent of Australian men say they don't want children, an increase from 11 per cent in 2005. Ian says his own childhood played a large part in his decision.

items.title: Why 'narcissist' bosses are more likely to oppose work from home
items.description: Research published last month found narcissistic leaders — those with a tendency to be self-centred and entitled — were more likely than others to resist remote work. Why? The study concluded "it interferes with their motivations for power and status".

items.title: The discipline behind royal wedding cellist's success
items.description: Sheku Kanneh-Mason went viral performing at Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's wedding. He's captivated audiences since and is touring Australia this month.

items.title: Australian EV owners deal with 'range anxiety'. China has almost eliminated it
items.description: You can swap an empty electric vehicle battery in about four minutes in China. It is part of how China has come to dominate the EV industry.

items.title: Mayor who provided character reference to sex offender resigns
items.description: Wyndham mayor Preet Singh says he showed "poor judgement" but also claims to have faced "abuse and intimidation" over the issue.

items.title: How authorities failed to heed one woman's reports of WA's worst child rapist
items.description: Maggie Dawkins's efforts to shine a light on the horrific abuses committed by Dennis McKenna against a generation of boys in Katanning are set down in a new book.

items.title: Firewood side hustle sparks multi-million-dollar business in four states
items.description: When bushfire and drought robbed farmer Peter Chauncy of his livelihood, he started chopping wood to sell. Forty years later, he runs one of Australia's largest firewood businesses.

items.title: Vaughters says night tests would have saved cycling '25 years of drama'
items.description: A former cyclist who took performance-enhancing drugs, now a team boss at the Tour de France, supports doping tests in the middle of the night at cycling's biggest race.

items.title: Man found not guilty of murder with scooter during street fight
items.description: A jury finds that Kane Flanders acted in self-defence when he struck Ash Morgan over the head with a Razor scooter at Raymond Terrace in 2024.

items.title: 'Sit down!' Joyce's dog interrupts 7.30 interview as he defends Hanson
items.description: The One Nation MP says Pauline Hanson's meeting with far-right British activist Tommy Robinson did not amount to an endorsement of his criminal conduct, rejecting suggestions she had crossed a "red line". The otherwise serious 7.30 interview was twice interrupted by Mr Joyce's dog, prompting him to yell at it to "sit down".

items.title: Medical clinic waited months to tell patients of data breach
items.description: Patients at a medical clinic in Brisbane's north only found out about the data breach almost three months after it was targeted by hackers.

items.title: South Australians urged to consider occasional power outages to curb costs
items.description: The driving force behind skyrocketing power prices this century has been investment by grid owners, and sometimes over-investment, but one expert believes it's time to start questioning our priorities if we want to reduce costs.
